{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-mt-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"50e00a4daea9b5fefdd8942a13e2d621225c97d817d34fde8acc38f03d1399bf","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-mt-class-d:lineage:46","source_registry_sha256":"35425fc1b75886d4bce9129f5de9443ae8cee634cff4a62363bbcd7cc017fe32","source_liveness_sha256":"bf7b5d7e97593e3a1c6181f4785c9171cedac6e24ab65da907a644a4b4907add"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Space management","heading":"C — Space management","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Space management

FACT_ID: sec11-F01 | anchor: A01
Choose a speed that always allows a safe stop within the clear view ahead. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec11-F02 | anchor: A01
For the four-second sight-distance check, choose the farthest clearly visible stationary object and slow down if you reach it before finishing a four-second count. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec11-F03 | anchor: A01
The four-second sight-distance check also helps a driver avoid outdriving the headlights at night. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec11-F04 | anchor: A01
Obey posted speed limits even when the road looks free of visible hazards. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec11-F05 | anchor: A01
Posted limits assume ideal conditions; wet or icy roads, poor visibility or heavy traffic require a slower speed. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec11-F06 | anchor: A01
Driving below the posted limit can still lead to a citation if the speed is too fast for conditions. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec11-F07 | anchor: A01
Keeping more room around the vehicle gives more time to react to other road users. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec11-F08 | anchor: A01
For the three-second following check, start counting when the rear of the vehicle ahead passes a fixed marker. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec11-F09 | anchor: A01
If you pass that marker before counting three seconds, fall back and repeat the check until the gap is at least three seconds. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec11-F10 | anchor: A02
Some conditions call for more following space, and the handbook suggests a four-second interval in these situations. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec11-F11 | anchor: A02
On slippery roads, leave more space ahead because stopping requires more distance. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec11-F12 | anchor: A02
When a following driver wants to pass, slow enough to create room ahead and help the pass finish sooner. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec11-F13 | anchor: A02
Give a motorcycle extra following room so a fallen rider can be avoided. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec11-F14 | anchor: A02
Motorcycles are especially likely to fall on wet, icy, gravel or metal surfaces such as bridge gratings and tracks. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec11-F15 | anchor: A02
Fall back when following a truck, bus, van or towing vehicle whose driver may not see you directly behind it. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec11-F16 | anchor: A02
A heavy load or trailer increases stopping distance, so leave more following room. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec11-F17 | anchor: A02
Increase the following gap when darkness or bad weather makes the view ahead difficult. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec11-F18 | anchor: A02
When closely followed, slow to encourage a pass or use a turnout to let the other driver by. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec11-F19 | anchor: A02
Allow emergency vehicles extra operating room when following them. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec11-F20 | anchor: A02
Approaching a railroad crossing, leave extra room behind buses or hazardous-material vehicles that must stop there. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec11-F21 | anchor: A02
When stopped on a hill, leave room for the vehicle ahead to roll backward as it starts. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec11-F22 | anchor: A02
A steady speed and early slowing signals help the driver behind maintain space. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec11-F23 | anchor: A02
For passenger pickup or drop-off, try to stop safely outside the traffic stream. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec11-F24 | anchor: A02
Before parallel parking with traffic approaching from behind, signal, draw alongside the space and let following vehicles pass. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec11-F25 | anchor: A02
If necessary slow driving holds up other cars, pull aside safely and let them pass. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec11-F26 | anchor: A02
If a tailgater follows and a right lane is available, move into that lane. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec11-F27 | anchor: A02
Without a right lane, wait for a clear way and reduce speed gradually to encourage the tailgater to pass. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec11-F28 | anchor: A02
Do not brake suddenly to discourage a tailgater, because that increases rear-impact risk. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec11-F29 | anchor: A02
Avoid remaining beside other vehicles on a multilane road; move ahead or fall behind to keep side room. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec11-F30 | anchor: A02
On a two-lane road, avoid crowding the centerline and generally travel near the middle of your lane. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec11-F31 | anchor: A02
On a road with at least two lanes, move over for entering traffic if the adjacent lane is unoccupied. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec11-F32 | anchor: A02
Leave extra space beside parked vehicles because a person or vehicle may move into your path. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0075]

Misconceptions: Sight distance, following distance and a temporary merging gap are different checks; a turn signal alone does not confirm a vehicle will turn.
Mnemonics: Authored cue: see, space, wait, pass only when clear.
Glossary: Sight distance; following interval; tailgater; median; space cushion; slow-moving emblem.
Dynamic facts: Posted limits and any external postal-equipment requirement need current applicable authority; no new universal safe-gap guarantee is created.
